title: EGamersWorld match pages answer HTTP 403 to the GitHub runner while a browser read returns the same prices
detail: The read-only probe in scripts/3877d48d_probe.py requested ten EGamersWorld match pages from ubuntu-24.04 at 2026-10-24T16:26Z and every one returned HTTP 403 (evidence: data/research/3877d48d/probe.json). The same pages answered with prices to a browser-class read in the same session. The 14:24Z build still resolved one EGamersWorld aggregated-reference row (1082858), so the block is new or intermittent. Consequence: the reference rung can silently fail on a runner, and a 403 is not evidence that no market exists. Recorded, not worked around.

title: Four unrelated EGamersWorld match pages display the same 1.80 / 1.80 pair
detail: Acend–UNiTY (1082996), Rooster–Abyssal (1082861), HOTU–The Huns (1082792) and 5star–1WIN (1082793) each display 1.80 for both teams at 2026-10-24T16:2xZ. Four unrelated fixtures cannot all carry an even-money two-sided bookmaker average, so the pair is refused under the existing identical-decimal placeholder rule. Nothing was priced from it; all four fixtures remain on their research-model picks.

title: A 1.001 near-lock quote was published as “1.00”, which reads as a zero-payout price
detail: FlyQuest–Staqued (1082860) is priced from a Thunderpick/Bovada quote of 1.001 / 12.00. scripts/build.py::observed_price_label formatted both sides with two decimals, so the phone summary and the register showed “line 1.00 / 12.00”. Fixed in this session: decimal_price() keeps three decimals below 1.10 (rendering 1.001 / 12.00) and leaves every ordinary price unchanged. The probability, the pick and the stored quote are untouched; the register now also states that a winning bet on a sub-1.02 quote returns under 2%.

title: The Bovada pages behind two published picks sit under a “series-11” path while Hotspawn lists CCT Europe Series #12
detail: The published source URLs for Spirit Academy–LFO 10 (1081156, provider name “Sokerorg”) and FORZE Reload–ex-RUSTEC (1081158) both live under /cct-europe/series-11/ in Bovada's own URL, while Hotspawn lists both in CCT Europe 2026 Series #12. A provider path segment is not proof that the wrong fixture was priced — the same provider labels unrelated fixtures the same way — so neither pick was changed. The mismatch is published for review instead of being silently rewritten.

title: A live Polymarket series event binds to Acend–UNiTY at the exact start time, but the published trail says no unique fixture was found
detail: Polymarket event 1238703 (cs2-ace1-unity-2026-10-25) is active and its own eventStartTime is 2026-10-25T09:00:00Z, exactly the Hotspawn start for 1082996. The published research trail for that fixture says “No unique exact-name, exact-start-time fixture”. The event's map-1 book is 0.03 / 0.97 (spread 0.94), so it may well still be refused on the spread ceiling — but the reason recorded is the wrong one. Request for the owning session: retry the series book for 1238703 instead of treating the fixture as unlisted. Nothing was repriced here.

title: The Valve-rating model is much more confident than HLTV's own estimate on HOTU–The Huns
detail: The published pick for HOTU–The Huns (1082792) is HOTU 94.1% from the uncalibrated Valve-rating model. HLTV's own page for the same fixture displays 77.1% HOTU / 22.9% The Huns. HLTV's figure is HLTV's estimate, not a betting line, so it is not used as an input and no probability was changed. The gap is published because a 17-point difference between an uncalibrated model and an independent public estimate is exactly what a reader should be able to see.

title: A publisher-wiring test was pinned to a fixed 06:30Z capture time and failed every run after ~14:30Z — already fixed on main by an injected clock
detail: tests/test_a5b59ee6_publisher_wiring.py called scripts.originate.run (which judged freshness against the real clock, eight hours) with a capture stamped 2026-10-24T06:20:00Z. Both end-to-end tests passed in the morning and failed on this session's 16:2xZ run with “the capture priced nothing”. This session first repaired it with a real-clock capture stamp; before merge, main received the better fix from session 5f9d0082 (commit 10d79ba): originate.run takes an injected now=NOW, so the whole chain is evaluated at a fixed instant and cannot rot after eight hours. This session adopted main's version and dropped its own patch — the flag is kept as the dated record of the failure class. Verified on the merged tree: python -m unittest tests.test_a5b59ee6_publisher_wiring → 10 tests OK.

title: Every active fixture has a pick; 10 of 23 come from a non-featured source
detail: The 2026-10-24T14:24:32Z snapshot lists 84 records, 23 open, 23 with a directional pick and 0 unresolved. Of those 23, 13 are featured market lines and 10 are fallback: 5 single-bookmaker, 1 aggregated reference and 4 research models (5 consensus rows also exist in the checked-in replay fixture). The separate fallback register now lists the money-backed fallback rows with their source, price and limit, and links the research-model rows to their existing register, so a reader can tell which picks rest on a real outside price.
